title: Behavior delta between two compatibility profiles
description: The difference between two PowerShell versions expressed as data, so the site can answer 'what would this script do differently on 7.7?' without anyone re-reading a changelog. Generated by diffing two profiles, then annotated by hand with migration guidance.

implemented.description: Changes BrowserShell emulates: implementation is implemented or verified.

documented.description: Changes recorded and cited but not emulated at all.

partial.description: Changes the engine models only in part.

subject.description: What changed: a command name, a behavior key, an automatic variable, or an engine area.

behaviorKey.description: The single profile key, when this change has exactly one. Null for none and for a derived family; read behaviorKeys instead.

behaviorKeys.description: Every profile key this change declares. A per-cmdlet switch fix expands to one key per parameter.

scope.description: Where the behaviour applies. `command: null` is an explicit claim that the change really is engine-wide, not a default.

documentedValue.description: What upstream does. Recorded whatever we emulate.

emulatedValue.description: What a command can actually read. Null when nothing is emulated — the split that keeps a documented change out of execution.

sources.description: Every upstream PR this record cites. Exactly one has role `primary` — the PR that made the change. `docs` is prose we could not confirm in a diff, kept visible as prose rather than laundered into a PR citation. `covers` records what the PR was READ to contain, so a later reader can tell a citation from a guess.

upstreamPr.description: The primary source's PR number, denormalised for links.

migration.description: What a script author should do. Required for impact=script-breaking.

conformanceFixture.description: Path to the fixture proving BrowserShell reproduces this difference. A script-breaking change without a fixture is unproven.

implementation.description: How much of the difference BrowserShell reproduces. The authored truth; `implemented` is its boolean projection.

partialityNote.description: Required when implementation is partial: what is missing.

evidence.description: Repo-relative paths proving the emulation. Non-empty and existing on disk whenever implementation is implemented or verified; at least one must be a test.

implemented.description: Derived from implementation, never authored. False means documented but not emulated; the UI must say so rather than imply fidelity.
